maria_cs: Hey team — drafting a short customer-facing ops playbook for Acme about caching, batching, and streaming during onboarding. Want to make it action-oriented (can run checks, paste config, quick rollback steps). Sharing draft below, PTAL before I send.

maria_cs: DRAFT START:
- Goal: keep 95th pct latency < 350ms while onboarding steady traffic (~8 rps) and avoid cold-start token spikes.
- Quick checklist for customers:
  1) Enable prefix KV caching for common prompts (esp. login/metadata prompts).
  2) Set conservative batching window for low-latency paths, aggressive for background tasks.
  3) Use streaming for interactive flows; fallback to non-streamed for bulk exports.
  4) Instrument early: token-level metrics and per-route SLA.

- Example recommended config (customer-facing snippet):
```yaml
cache: 
  prefix_kv: true
  ttl_seconds: 300
batching:
  latency_slo_ms: 350
  max_wait_ms: 25   # start small during onboarding
  max_batch_size: 16
streaming:
  enabled: true
  chunk_size: 512
```

- Quick validation steps for CS/Dev: run these locally before going live:
  - curl health endpoint: `curl -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health`
  - generate 50 warmup requests with `ab` or `wrk` to verify latency tail
  - verify cache hits in Console (Routes -> Cache hits) after warmup

- Rollback knobs for customers:
  - Disable batching: set `max_wait_ms: 0`
  - Turn off prefix_kv if stale: `prefix_kv: false`
  - Route to smaller model if latency spikes: `model_override: small-llama-v2`

- Enablement agenda (15m):
  - 0-5m: quick metrics walkthrough (latency, token cost, cache hit rate)
  - 5-10m: demo changing batching/window and immediate effect
  - 10-15m: Q&A + action items (who flips which switch)

- Feedback capture: ask customer to run this quick survey after first 24h: `How responsive did it feel? (1-5)`, `Any outputs degraded? Y/N`, `Anything you changed?`
DRAFT END

zahra_eng: This is a really solid start. A couple of small suggestions: call out the telemetry keys we expect in Console (e.g., `route.latency.p95`, `route.cache.hit_rate`, `route.batch.size_avg`) so CS can point customers exactly where to look. Also add a short snippet for a streaming client example.

maria_cs: Good call. I'll add telemetry keys. Can you drop a streaming example?

zahra_eng: Sure — tiny js snippet to show streaming consumption:
```js
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({model: 'chat-xl', stream: true, prompt: 'Hello'}),
});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true){
  const {done, value} = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  process.stdout.write(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
}
```

daniel_csm: Adding to the enablement agenda: allocate 5 extra minutes to confirm renewal health signals — e.g., feature usage, monthly token spend ramp, and any open blockers. If we see token spend < 30% of expected during first week, flag for follow-up.

maria_cs: Good point. I'll add a renewal-risk checklist item: low usage, high error rate, or repeated manual rollbacks -> trigger AE outreach.

ryan_prod: Quick product note: recommend customers use quantization profile Q4 for latency-sensitive paths; we'll document quality tradeoffs. Also suggest adding a fallback model alias (e.g., `customer-acme-fallback`) so routing can switch without changing app code.

sre-bot: deploy:prefetch-runbook v1.3 applied to `customer-success/playbooks` by zahra_eng at 1991234574 :white_check_mark:

priya_acme: Thanks @maria_cs, this looks actionable. A couple of questions from our side:
- For TTL on prefix cache, is 5min safe for session-bound prompts?
- When you say "warmup requests", how many do you recommend for 8 rps steady traffic?

maria_cs: @priya_acme great q's — for session prompts 5min is a decent default; if your session content changes a lot drop to 60–120s. For warmup, run 2x your expected concurrency for 60s (so at 8 rps steady, do a 1 minute run at ~16 rps). We'll include a one-liner script in the email.
